cards.back: All points through which an attacker can interact with a system: ports, services, identities, code, third parties, exposed data.
Product no longer supported by the vendor: no patches, no security updates.
Patch available but not applied: known and exploitable flaw.
Technology superseded by a newer version, with incompatibilities and legacy dependencies.
Outside inventory and management tools: no one patches or monitors it.
Every open port is an exposed interface; a forgotten service widens the attack surface.
Hypervisor, unpatched VMs, lateral movement between guests, or sandbox escape.
Flaw unknown to the vendor with no patch available: reduce attack surface and detect behavior.
Weak algorithm (MD5, SHA-1, 3DES), short key, obsolete TLS, or poor key management.
Time of Check (TOC) and Time of Use (TOU) separated in time; the attacker alters state in between.
Compromised update distributed through the vendor's legitimate channel.
Password or API key written in code: replace with a secrets vault and rotation.
Verbose errors that expose paths, queries, or credentials.
Forgotten accounts and unauthorized devices plugged into the network: persistent access.
Service used without security approval, outside inventory and monitoring.
IdP = central authentication and token service; mobile = apps, permissions, and local storage.
Public bucket, open port, excessive permissions, or unchanged default setting.
LLM = prompt injection and data leakage; public repo = exposed secrets; public object storage = bucket accessible without auth.
